CANONICAL_NAME.value: BASIC Computer Games (David Ahl, 1978): HAMURABI and SUPER STAR TREK -- original BASIC listings run under Bywater BASIC

value.lineage: The hobbyist BASIC culture of the 1970s: HAMURABI (a resource-rationing simulation under scarcity and random plague/rat pressure, from DEC's 1968 'King'/'Sumer' via Ahl) and SUPER STAR TREK (Mayfield 1971; Leedom/Ahl 1974-78), the most-copied game program of its era. Preserved as the original line-numbered BASIC (from the coding-horror/basic-computer-games transcription of Ahl's book) and executed by Bywater BASIC 2.20, itself a 1990s interpreter of the classic dialect.

value.built_to: let a player govern a city for ten years by rationing grain between food, seed and land purchases under random harvests, rats and plague (HAMURABI); command a starship against Klingons with finite energy and torpedoes (STAR TREK)
value.pressure: scarcity (grain, energy), randomness, deadlines (ten years; stardates)
value.success_means: the program runs the simulation to its end state and reports it; the classic dialect executes under a later interpreter

value.pressure: scarcity, random shocks, hard time limit
value.failure_condition: starve the people -> impeachment; run out of energy -> destruction

value: derived_from: DEC 'The Sumer Game' (Dyment 1968) / Ahl's HAMURABI (1973)

cut.note: two small resource games whose mechanism is a scoring rule over a stochastic resource loop: HAMURABI is a ten-round allocation problem (buy/sell land, feed, plant) with a uniform random yield, a rat loss on even yields, a plague with a fixed probability, population growth from stored grain, and an impeachment rule on starvation; STAR TREK is a grid game where every action costs energy from a shared budget and every hit is a random fraction of the energy committed. They are worlds, not organisms: the cut records the pressure each defines

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade); HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_MIRROR -> CONTEMPORARY_COPY per FILE by Techne's #387 ASK 2 ruling (2026-09-18: a source type, not a grade); tree-level RECONSTRUCTION caveat where the mirror is a git history assembled after the fact (unix-history-repo); ruled for odepack-netlib / bsd-tcp-4.2-1983 / compact-4.2bsd-1983 and applied to the other archive-mirror records by the same reasoning until TECHNE-89 issues per-record blocks

organs.human_name: hammurabi.bas: 310 (land price 17-26), 800 (C = RND*5+1 yield / rats / babies), 515-533 (harvest, rats when C even: E = S/C, immigrants), 540-555 (fed = Q/20; starved D; impeach if D > 0.45 P), 542 (plague: Q < 0 with probability 0.15), 860-896 (final grading by starvation percent and acres per person)
organs.mechanism: each year: report; halve the population on a plague (15 percent); price land at 17-26 per acre (uniform); take buy/sell, feed and plant decisions, each validated against stock, acreage and one tender per ten acres; draw one uniform 1-5 that serves as the yield per acre, then redraw: if the draw is even, rats eat stock/C; immigration = C * (20 A + S) / P / 100 + 1; people fed = Q/20; if more than 45 percent starve the game ends with impeachment; after ten years grade on average starvation percent and acres per person
organs.state: P, S, A, Y, and the two running tallies
assumptions: one uniform draw reused for yield, rats and immigration is enough randomness for a game; the grade thresholds (3, 10, 33 percent; 7, 9, 10 acres) define what good governance means
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the most copied 'resource management under uncertainty' toy of the era; every constant is visible
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the same draw C drives yield and immigration, so a bad harvest also means few immigrants (a correlation the player cannot see); plague is independent of everything

organs.human_name: superstartrek.bas: 370 (E = 3000, Klingons and stardates random), 475 (FNR), 2880-3000 (damage: a random device D(R1) gains or loses a random amount), 4250-4550 (phasers: X units split over Klingons, hit H = (X/K3 / distance) * (RND + 2), a hit below 15 percent of the target's energy is absorbed)
organs.mechanism: one energy pool pays for warp movement, shields and phaser fire; a phaser volley of X units is divided among the Klingons in the quadrant and scaled by inverse distance and a random factor in [2, 3); a hit smaller than 15 percent of the target's remaining energy does no damage; after actions, with probability 0.2 a random subsystem is damaged or repaired by a random amount, disabling the corresponding command until repaired; Klingons return fire when the ship moves
assumptions: a single budget makes every choice a trade-off; random subsystem damage forces plan changes
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the most copied game of the 1970s (the record); a budget-and-risk loop in 425 lines
organs.source_boundary: superstartrek.bas; CANDIDATE because read by grep, not line by line

rejected_cuts.candidate: the text of the reports, the input validation subroutines (710, 720), the galaxy setup and display code of Star Trek

rejected_cuts.evidence: the loop, the random draws and the grading rule are separable constants and could be varied independently

pressures.condition: an organism controls three allocations per round of a stock that grows by a random multiplier; a rare catastrophe halves the population; the score punishes any single year above a starvation threshold (game over) and grades the average; the horizon is ten rounds
pressures.failure_condition: impeachment (one year over 45 percent starvation) or a low grade
pressures.world_punishes: maximising expected growth without a reserve (one bad draw ends the game); hoarding (low grade)
pressures.world_rewards: a reserve sized to the worst plausible draw
pressures.observable_consequence: grade distribution over seeds for greedy, fixed-reserve and adaptive-reserve policies; probability of impeachment per policy
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given next year's draw must never be impeached and score 'fantastic'; a greedy organism must show impeachments in the seed distribution; the adaptive reserve must sit between: the world must show all three
